what_its_for: Mefloquine is used to prevent and treat malaria, a serious infection spread by mosquito bites. It works by killing the parasite that causes malaria in your body. It is most often used by travelers going to areas where malaria is common.
how_to_take: Take mefloquine by mouth with at least 8 ounces (240 mL) of water. Always take it with food to help reduce stomach upset. Swallow the tablet whole. Do not crush or chew the tablet. Try to take it on the same day each week if using it for prevention. Take it at the same time each day to help you remember.
dosing: For PREVENTION of malaria: Adults typically take one 250 mg tablet once a week. Start taking it 1 to 2 weeks BEFORE traveling to a malaria-risk area, continue taking it DURING your trip, and keep taking it for 4 weeks AFTER you leave the area. For TREATMENT of malaria: The dose is higher and is taken all at once or split into two doses. Your doctor will tell you exactly how many tablets to take. Always follow your doctor's instructions — do not take more or less than prescribed.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose for prevention (weekly dosing), take it as soon as you remember. Then go back to your regular weekly schedule. Do not take two doses on the same day to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store mefloquine at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep it out of reach of children and pets. Do not use it after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking mefloquine, as it can make side effects like dizziness worse. Do not drive, operate heavy machinery, or do activities that require alertness until you know how this medicine affects you — it can cause dizziness, confusion, or problems with balance. Avoid taking mefloquine with certain heart medications (such as quinine or quinidine) or certain antibiotics (such as halofantrine) without your doctor's approval. Tell all your doctors and dentist that you take mefloquine before any new medications are prescribed.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: severe anxiety, depression, restlessness, or unusual changes in mood or behavior; hallucinations (seeing or hearing things that are not there); seizures (convulsions); thoughts of harming yourself; severe dizziness or loss of balance; irregular heartbeat or pounding heartbeat; ringing in the ears or sudden hearing loss; vision changes; or a skin rash with blistering. Also call your doctor if you develop a fever during or after travel to a malaria-risk area, even after you have stopped taking mefloquine.
when_it_works: For PREVENTION: Mefloquine starts building protection in your body about 1 to 2 weeks after you begin taking it, which is why you must start it before your trip. It will continue to protect you during and for 4 weeks after your trip. For TREATMENT: Mefloquine begins working quickly to fight the malaria infection, but it may take a few days before you start feeling better. Complete the full course as prescribed even if you feel well.
special_populations: PREGNANCY: Mefloquine should generally be avoided in the first trimester of pregnancy if possible. Talk to your doctor — in some high-risk situations, it may still be recommended. BREASTFEEDING: Small amounts of mefloquine pass into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding while on this medicine. CHILDREN: Mefloquine can be used in children, but the dose is based on body weight. Follow your doctor's instructions carefully. ELDERLY: Older adults may be more sensitive to side effects, especially dizziness and heart-related effects. Talk to your doctor. MENTAL HEALTH CONDITIONS: Mefloquine should NOT be used if you have a history of depression, anxiety disorders, schizophrenia, psychosis, or seizures (epilepsy). Tell your doctor about any mental health history before starting this medicine. HEART CONDITIONS: Tell your doctor if you have any heart rhythm problems before taking mefloquine.
